Full details: Title check

**Explanation** The title names the Gemini default-model change (small-fast and haiku fallback to gemini-3.1-flash-lite), which matches the diff across model.ts, configs.ts, and the test file. It is concise and scoped. It uses a conventional fix(gemini) prefix and the title is 81 characters, which is on the long side but still descriptive.
Full details: Description check

**Explanation** The description follows the template. It has Summary (what and why), Impact (user-facing and developer/maintainer), Testing (validation checklist, commands and results, CI status pending), and Notes (provider path tested, screenshots not applicable, follow-up work). It explains the deprecation reason and the test results. The 'Fixes `#N`' line is an unfilled placeholder, and the template's 'for follow-ups' line was dropped, which are minor issues. **Resolution** Non-blocking: replace the 'Fixes `#N`' placeholder with the real issue number, or remove it if no issue exists.
Full details: Risk Surface Disclosed

**Explanation** The PR touches a risk surface. It changes the Gemini default model in `getSmallFastModel()` and `getDefaultHaikuModel()` (src/utils/model/model.ts, lines 93 and 367). Both functions feed background and provider-routed calls, such as hooks, session titles, away summaries, the bash classifier, and WebSearch (verified by grep). The check therefore applies. The risk surface is disclosed. The PR description states that: - With the Gemini provider and no `GEMINI_MODEL`, small/fast calls and `haiku` now use `gemini-3.1-flash-lite`. - The new model is priced above the retired `gemini-2.0-flash-lite`. - `GEMINI_MODEL` still takes precedence. - Validation is unit-test only. No live Gemini API call was made. - The Gemini sonnet-tier mappings are unchanged. No blocker is introduced. The diff changes only fallback and mapping strings (src/utils/model/configs.ts and model.ts). The replacement model already appears in the Gemini catalog (src/integrations/models/gemini.ts line 41 and src/integrations/brands/gemini.ts line 16). The supplied current review returned zero actionable findings. It did not add its own callout, so the disclosure rests on the PR description. Non-blocking notes: - The claim that Google retired `gemini-2.0-flash-lite` on June 1, 2026 rests on the cited Google deprecations page. I could not check that page in this run. - The pricing impact on background calls is a cost change for Gemini users. The author discloses it but does not quantify it.
Full details: No Hidden Policy Change

**Explanation** The PR changes a routing default, but the change is disclosed and is not hidden in cleanup. Evidence: - The committed diff touches only three files: `src/utils/model/model.ts`, `src/utils/model/configs.ts`, and `src/utils/model/model.openai-shim-providers.test.ts`. - In `model.ts`, the Gemini fallback in `getSmallFastModel()` and `getDefaultHaikuModel()` changes from `gemini-2.0-flash-lite` to `gemini-3.1-flash-lite`. `GEMINI_MODEL` still takes precedence. - In `configs.ts`, the Gemini haiku entries in `GEMINI_MODEL_DEFAULTS`, `CLAUDE_3_5_HAIKU_CONFIG`, and `CLAUDE_HAIKU_4_5_CONFIG` change to match. No other provider mapping changes. - The title, PR description, and summary all state the routing-default change. The description also states the cost impact ("priced above the retired 2.0 Flash-Lite") and the reason (the upstream deprecation). - The change does not touch trust model, telemetry/network, or permission policy. Non-blocking note: the change alters the default model for Gemini background and haiku calls, and it raises cost. Maintainers should confirm they accept this default swap. The PR states the change openly, so this does not make it a hidden policy change.
